title: Session token amortization experiments
content:
Purpose / quick summary:
- Back-of-envelope testing of amortizing expensive context tokens (system+init) over a session to inform starter and pay-as-you-go credits.
- Goal: propose 2 simple heuristics we can A/B that are cheap to implement server-side and explainable to customers.

Context / motivation:
- Many interactive apps pay a heavy fixed token cost per session (system + persona + seed). For short sessions this dominates.
- We want starter credits and microtiers that don't over-subsidize heavy users but also don't punish quick wins (chatty prototypes).
- Current alternatives: flat per-token, per-request minimum, session-bucket credits, decay-over-time. Each has upsides/complexities.

Assumptions (engineer to finance priors):
- Backend cost: average model compute cost ~= $0.0009 per token served (hosted cost after infra margins) for gen-capable model family X (median).
- Avg user session: 3 roundtrips, 2.2k tokens total (including system), median 1.1k user-visible tokens.
- System prompt overhead: 600 tokens used on session start (system + persona + tool scaffolding).
- KV-cache + batching improvements reduce incremental gen cost ~30% for subsequent calls after first in session for warm routes. (This is heuristic).

Heuristic A: "Amortized fixed" (simple linear amortization)
- Charge full tokens consumed, but subtract an "amortized system credit" per session: system_credit = min(system_cost, floor(system_tokens / expected_roundtrips))
- Implementation: when session is opened, mark system_tokens S. For each request i with T_i tokens consumed, bill T_i - floor(S / max(1, expected_roundtrips_per_session)). expected_roundtrips_per_session = 3 (configurable global default).
- Example math: S=600, expected_roundtrips=3 => subtract 200 tokens from each of first 3 requests. If only 1 request happens, only 200 is subtracted once (client still pays 400 of system).
- Pros: easy to explain, bounded subsidy, lowers friction for 1–3 turn sessions.
- Cons: users can game by doing many small requests up to expected_roundtrips; need ceiling and per-session cap.

Heuristic B: "Decay credit" (time-decay amortization)
- Apply full system_credit on first request, then exponentially decay leftover credit by factor 0.5 per subsequent request within TTL (e.g., 30min idle).
- Billing formula: billed = max(0, tokens - credit_current); credit_current = credit_prev * decay + (maybe add small top-up for new tool state)
- Example math: S=600, request1 T1=800 -> credit covers 600 => bill 200. Remaining credit 0. request2 within 10m T2=300 -> credit regenerated = 600*0.5=300 => covers T2 fully => bill 0. Request3 after 40m TTL expired -> no credit.
- Pros: favors sticky sessions, harder to game repeatedly because credit decays. More intuitive UX: "we cover persona leakage for short chats".
- Cons: slightly more complex server logic and edge cases with multi-device sessions.

Quick scenarios (numbers):
- Tiny trial: 1 request only, average tokens=1k (includes systems).
  - Baseline per-token: bill 1000 tokens -> cost ~ $0.90 (host cost) -> customer sees 1000 credits.
  - Heuristic A amortized: subtract 200 -> bill 800 -> customer sees ~800 credits (20% cheaper).
  - Heuristic B decay: first request get full 600 covered -> bill 400 -> customer sees 400 credits (big subsidy).
  - Observation: B favors conversion for single-request trials; A is middle ground.

- Medium session (3 rounds, tokens 2.4k, S=600):
  - Baseline: bill 2400 tokens.
  - A: subtract 200 each for first 3 => subtract 600 total -> bill 1800.
  - B: first request covers large fraction then decays; approximate bill ~1300–1500 depending on distribution.

- Abuse case: bot that spins 3x tiny requests repeatedly to drain credits.
  - Need glue: per-session cap on total amortized tokens (e.g., cap system_credit to 600/session), rate limit (per-user per-minute), and require session creation (auth) to be non-trivial (e.g., anti-abuse token).

Mapping to product suggestions:
- Starter free credits: present credits as token-equivalent but show "session buffer" on first N sessions via heuristic B for onboarding flows (e.g., first 10 sessions get stronger decay factor 0.66).
- PAYG: default to Heuristic A with expected_roundtrips=3; makes book-keeping trivial and predictable for billing teams.
- Micro-tier monthly: provide a fixed monthly session-bucket (e.g., 200 session-buffers of 600-token amortized value) + residual per-token billing for heavy tails.

Unit economics quick calc (rough):
- Suppose 10k starter users use the product, avg 2 sessions in trial, median 1k tokens/session. If we use Heuristic B and cover 60% of system tokens on first hit: average subsidy per user = 1 session * 600*0.6 = 360 tokens -> host cost ~360 * $0.0009 = $0.32 per new user. For 10k users -> $3.2k cost to onboarding; seems acceptable for acquisition if conversion lift > 0.5%.

Experiment ideas (easy -> medium)
- A1 (easy): Implement Heuristic A server-side flag for a subset of traffic (10%), expected_roundtrips=3, cap system_credit=600. Metrics: session length distribution, median tokens/billed, conversion from free->paid at 7d.
- B1 (medium): Decay credit within 30m TTL for 10% traffic. Track abuse signals, multi-device sessions, and effect on starter conversion.
- Pricing UX experiment: show "session buffer used: X/600 tokens" in dashboard for first 30 days to teach customers how amortization works (hypothesis: transparency reduces unexpected billing inquiries).

Open questions / risks:
- Multi-device continuity: when a user opens same session from phone+web we may double-subtract credit if we anchor per-device. Anchor per-session-id instead but requires session model in API.
- Accounting complexity: need to map amortized token discounts to invoice lines; prefer to expose charged_tokens and system_subsidy fields. That is okay but requires billing pipeline change.
- Edge-case with function/tool calls where system tokens are split across tool inputs; need deterministic way to assign system_tokens S.
- Legal/compliance: show clear TOS language about credits and abuse.

Next steps / quick roadmap:
- Sync with billing (Marisol) to check feasibility of new invoice fields (charged_tokens, subsidy_tokens).
- Spike: dev 1 week to implement Heuristic A toggle + metrics. Run 2 weeks internal, then 4-week public A/B.
- If A wins (improved conversion with acceptable unit cost), iterate on B and study decay params.
- Add simple UX prototype showing session buffer in Console for pilot customers.

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Ask SRE about session-id retention TTL and cost for session state (affects decision A vs B).
- Create PRIC-xxx ticket to track cap/rate-limits; include expected worst-case subsidy burn calc.
- Draft short one-pager for growth with sample math (use numbers above) and include recommended default: Heuristic A for PAYG, Heuristic B for Onboarding pilot.

Rough back-of-envelope numbers summary:
- Host cost per token: $0.0009
- System prompt S: 600 tokens
- Expected_roundtrips default: 3 (A)
- Heuristic A subsidy per 3-round session: 600 tokens -> $0.54 host cost
- Heuristic B potential subsidy (single-request heavy): up to 600 tokens -> $0.54 host cost

End of scratchpad.

-- Asha
